title: Your Stance on the Facts: Adverbs Like En Realidad

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *lamentablemente*, *en realidad* and *en rigor* from B2 Unit 1: stance adverbs that comment on a whole sentence. They are useful for the story of two languages in Paraguay, where people often assume things that are not exactly true. Here they correct an idea, show how sure you are or give the exact fact.

sections.title: Stance adverbs at work
rows: En realidad, Paraguay tiene dos lenguas oficiales.
*en realidad*: you correct what someone assumed
Indudablemente, el guaraní forma parte de la vida diaria.
En rigor, el guaraní es lengua oficial desde 1992.
*en rigor*: strictly speaking, the exact fact
Lamentablemente, algunos hablantes sienten vergüenza de mezclar las lenguas.

items.spanish: En realidad, Paraguay tiene dos lenguas oficiales.
items.english: In fact, Paraguay has two official languages.

items.spanish: Indudablemente, el guaraní forma parte de la vida diaria.
items.english: Undoubtedly, Guaraní is part of daily life.

items.spanish: En rigor, el guaraní es lengua oficial desde 1992.
items.english: Strictly speaking, Guaraní has been an official language since 1992.

items.spanish: Los hablantes, indudablemente, cambian de lengua según la situación.
items.english: Speakers, undoubtedly, change language depending on the situation.

sections.content: Remember the comma test: you can pause and put commas around a stance adverb. When you write about a language, use *en rigor* and *en realidad* for exact facts and keep a feeling like *lamentablemente* for what you really think; give the opinion to someone when it is history.
